content.title: About
content.content: Cream soda is a non‑alcoholic, lightly carbonated beverage with a sweet vanilla or creamy flavor. It is often used as a base for cocktails, dessert drinks, and in children's meals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first cream soda recipe appeared in the United States in the late 19th century.
Its traditional color is light‑brown or creamy, achieved by adding caramel.
In some countries it is served with a scoop of ice cream – the “float”.
Typical cream soda contains little to no caffeine.
Flavor is often enhanced with vanilla extract, nut‑derived aromatics, or a buttery note.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: Like any non‑alcoholic drink, cream soda contributes to the body’s fluid balance.

items.title: Quick energy source
items.content: Contains simple sugars that are rapidly absorbed, providing an immediate energy boost.

items.title: Culinary enhancer
items.content: Used in cooking to add sweetness and light carbonation to desserts and sauces.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Excessive consumption can lead to weight gain, tooth decay, and elevated blood glucose levels.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: The acidic nature may irritate the stomach in people with sensitivity.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: Some versions are flavored with nut or dairy extracts, which may trigger allergies.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Drink cream soda chilled, use it in cocktail mixes, add to ice cream, fruit salads, or incorporate into pancake batter for a light, airy texture.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep refrigerated and consume within 3‑5 days.
